## Part A: Examples of Conditional Statements

### Example A: if ... else

```{r}
score <- 78

if (score >= 75) {
  print("Passed")
} else {
  print("Failed")
}
```

### Example B: if ... else if ... else

```{r}
score <- 86

if (score >= 90) {
  print("Excellent")
} else if (score >= 80) {
  print("Good")
} else if (score >= 75) {
  print("Fair")
} else {
  print("Needs Improvement")
}
```

### Example C: ifelse() on a vector

```{r}
scores <- c(92, 68, 75, 81, 59)
ifelse(scores >= 75, "Passed", "Failed")
```

### Example D: combining conditions

```{r}
grade <- 91
attendance <- 95

if (grade >= 90 & attendance >= 90) {
  print("Honors candidate")
}
```

## Part B: Conditional Statements

### Question #1

```{r}
temp <- 33

if (temp >= 32) {
  print("Hot")
} else {
  print("Not hot")
}
```

### Question #2

```{r}
age <- 17

if (age < 13) {
  print("Child")
} else if (age <= 19) {
  print("Teenager")
} else {
  print("Adult")
}
```

### Question #3

```{r}
marks <- c(45, 88, 73, 100, 62)
result <- ifelse(marks >= 60, "Pass", "Fail")
print(result)
```

### Question #4

```{r}
x <- 10

if (x > 5) {
  print("A")
} else if (x > 8) {
  print("B")
} else {
  print("C")
}

# Answer:
# I expected "A", and that's what R printed.
# Since 10 is greater than 5, the first condition is already TRUE, so R runs
# that block and ignores everything after it. Even though 10 > 8 is also
# true, R never gets to that line.
```

### Question #5

Answer:

`if` looks at just one value and decides which block of code to run. `ifelse()` goes through a whole vector and gives back a result for each element. I'd use `if` when I need my script to make one decision, like whether to import a file. I'd use `ifelse()` when I want to label every row in a column, like marking each student as passed or failed.

## Part C: Importing the CSV File

### Question #6

Import the file safely, using if ... else to check that the file exists.

```{r}
file_name <- "students_grades.csv"

if (file.exists(file_name)) {
  grades <- read.csv(file_name, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  print("File imported.")
} else {
  stop("File not found. Save students_grades.csv in the same folder as this .Rmd file.")
}
```

Inspect the data.

```{r}
head(grades)
dim(grades)
str(grades)
summary(grades)
colSums(is.na(grades))
```

Answer the following.

```{r}
nrow(grades)
ncol(grades)
names(which(colSums(is.na(grades)) > 0))
class(grades$Section)
range(grades$Attendance)
```

Answer:

`grades` has 15 rows and 7 columns.
Only the Midterm column has a missing value, and there's just one NA.
Section is stored as character (text).
Attendance goes from a low of 70 up to a high of 100.

Check the structure.

```{r}
stopifnot(nrow(grades) == 15, ncol(grades) == 7, sum(is.na(grades)) == 1)
```

### Applying Conditional Statements

f.1 Compute the final grade.

```{r}
grades$FinalGrade <- 0.30 * grades$Quiz + 0.30 * grades$Midterm + 0.40 * grades$Final
grades[, c("Name", "FinalGrade")]
```

f.2 Pass or fail.

```{r}
grades$Result <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                 ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Passed", "Failed"))
table(grades$Result)
```

f.3 Grade remarks.

```{r}
grades$Remarks <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Incomplete",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 90, "Excellent",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85, "Very Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 80, "Good",
                  ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 75, "Fair", "Needs Improvement")))))
table(grades$Remarks)
```

f.4 Attendance flag.

```{r}
grades$AttendanceFlag <- ifelse(grades$Attendance < 80, "At Risk", "OK")
table(grades$AttendanceFlag)
```
f.5 Honors candidates.

```{r}
grades$Honors <- ifelse(!is.na(grades$FinalGrade) &
                        grades$FinalGrade >= 90 &
                        grades$Attendance >= 90, "Yes", "No")
table(grades$Honors)
```

f.6 if ... else if inside a loop.

```{r}
loop_remarks <- character(nrow(grades))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(grades))) {
  g <- grades$FinalGrade[i]

  if (is.na(g)) {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Incomplete"
  } else if (g >= 90) {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Excellent"
  } else if (g >= 85) {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Very Good"
  } else if (g >= 80) {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Good"
  } else if (g >= 75) {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Fair"
  } else {
    loop_remarks[i] <- "Needs Improvement"
  }
}

loop_remarks
```

f.7 The Console test.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
if (grades$FinalGrade >= 75) print("Passed")
```

Answer:

r gives the error "the condition has length > 1". That's because `grades$FinalGrade` has 15 values, so the comparison gives back 15 TRUE/FALSE results, but `if` can only handle a single TRUE or FALSE. The loop doesn't run into this problem because it hands `if` one grade at a time, and the `is.na()` check takes care of the missing grade before any comparison happens

f.8 Summarize your results.

```{r}
table(grades$Result)
table(grades$AttendanceFlag)
table(grades$Honors)

# Answer:
# 10 students passed.
# 4 students are At Risk because of low attendance.
# 4 students made it as honors candidates.
```

f.9 Column check.

```{r}
ncol(grades)
stopifnot(ncol(grades) == 12)
```

## Part D: Exporting Results to .csv

### Question #7

Export the full processed table.

```{r}
write.csv(grades, "students_grades_processed.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

Export the at-risk students.

```{r}
at_risk <- grades[grades$AttendanceFlag == "At Risk", ]

if (nrow(at_risk) > 0) {
  write.csv(at_risk, "at_risk_students.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No at-risk students. No file written.")
}
```

Export the honors list.

```{r}
honors <- grades[grades$Honors == "Yes",
                 c("StudentID", "Name", "Section", "FinalGrade", "Attendance")]

if (nrow(honors) > 0) {
  write.csv(honors, "honors_list.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No honors candidates this term.")
}
```

Verify your exports.

```{r}
check_all <- read.csv("students_grades_processed.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(check_all)
dim(grades)

check_risk <- read.csv("at_risk_students.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(check_risk)

check_honors <- read.csv("honors_list.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
dim(check_honors)
```

### Question #8

```{r}
write.csv(grades, "temp_with_rownames.csv")
temp_check <- read.csv("temp_with_rownames.csv")
names(temp_check)
dim(temp_check)
invisible(file.remove("temp_with_rownames.csv"))
```

Answer:

the missing midterm shows up as `NA` in the exported file, and that student's FinalGrade is `NA` too.

if I leave out `row.names = FALSE`, R adds an extra first column with the row numbers 1 to 15 and no header. When I read the file back in, R calls that column `X`, so I end up with 13 columns instead of 12, and the extra one doesn't hold any useful data.

### Question #9

a. Use nested ifelse() statements.

```{r}
grades$Scholarship <- ifelse(is.na(grades$FinalGrade), "Pending",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 95 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Full",
                      ifelse(grades$FinalGrade >= 85 & grades$Attendance >= 90, "Partial",
                             "None")))
```

c. Select students whose Scholarship is "Full" or "Partial".

```{r}
qualified <- grades[grades$Scholarship %in% c("Full", "Partial"), ]
qualified
```

Export them to scholarship_candidates.csv.

```{r}
if (nrow(qualified) > 0) {
  write.csv(qualified, "scholarship_candidates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  print("No students qualify for a scholarship.")
}
```

Print a count of each category.

```{r}
table(grades$Scholarship)
```

### Question #10

```{r}
# Answer:
# 1. Comparing NA to a number just gives NA, and if() can't work with NA.
#    Checking is.na() first lets me deal with the missing grade before comparing.
# 2. The student with the missing grade would get NA instead of "Incomplete"
#    since FinalGrade < 75 gives NA and ifelse() passes that NA along.
# 3. ifelse() is better when I want a result for every value in a column.
#    if ... else is better for a single value or for deciding which code runs.
# 4. It's the only way to be sure the export actually worked. I can check that
#    the rows and columns are right and that no extra row-number column was added.
```
